11 The IKAROS satellite has mass 320 kg and moves through space using a solar sail of area 20 m2.
The average solar wind pressure is 1.0 × 10–5
N m–2.
What is the acceleration of the satellite caused by the solar wind?
A
3.1 × 10–8
m s–2
B
6.3 × 10–7
m s–2
C
3.2 × 10–3
m s–2
D
6.4 × 10–2
m s–2

hints: Notice the solar wind pressure is $1.0 \times 10^{-5} \text{ N m}^{-2}$ acting on a sail of area $20 \text{ m}^2$, not a force on its own.
Recall pressure links force and area by $p = F/A$, so the sail force is $F = pA$, and then Newton's second law $F = ma$ gives the acceleration.
First work out $F = 1.0 \times 10^{-5} \times 20$ in $\text{N}$, then divide that small force by $320 \text{ kg}$ and check the power of ten for $\text{m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough: Identify the given data: $m = 320 \text{ kg}$, sail area $A = 20 \text{ m}^2$, solar wind pressure $p = 1.0 \times 10^{-5} \text{ N m}^{-2}$.
State the governing physics: pressure is force per unit area $p = F/A$, so $F = pA$, and the resulting motion follows $F = ma$, so $a = F/m$.
Calculate the total force on the sail: $F = (1.0 \times 10^{-5}) \times 20 = 2.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ N}$.
Calculate the acceleration: $a = F/m = (2.0 \times 10^{-4})/320 = 6.25 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Check units and size: $\text{N kg}^{-1}$ is $\text{m s}^{-2}$, and a tiny force on a large mass gives a tiny acceleration, about $6.3 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m s}^{-2}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: Calculates $p/m$ without the $20 \text{ m}^2$ sail area, treating pressure in $\text{N m}^{-2}$ as if it were already the force in $\text{N}$.

B.explanation: Uses $F = pA$ then $a = F/m$ to give $2.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ N}$ divided by $320 \text{ kg}$.

C.explanation: Calculates $p \times m = 3.2 \times 10^{-3}$, multiplying pressure by mass instead of using $F = pA$ and $a = F/m$.

D.explanation: Calculates $p \times A \times m = 6.4 \times 10^{-2}$, multiplying by mass instead of dividing the sail force by mass.
